messages:
anya: Heads-up, found a deploy config with a... creative version string: `version: 0.0.1.0.0-kale`
jules: lol what did the package eat to become that version?
ravi: that's not semver, that's a crunchy timestamp
anya: snippet: ```yaml
app:
  name: kale-crunch
  version: 0.0.1.0.0-kale
  enabled: true
```
jules: parser output: "I expected 3 numbers, got a salad." :rofl:
ops-bot: Rolling deploy scheduled for 09:30 — note: version string does not match schema (reaction: :warning:)
ravi: proposing a lint rule: `^v?\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-[a-zA-Z0-9]+)?(\+[a-z0-9]+)?$`
anya: either that or we automatically normalize to first-three-segments + build metadata so nothing explodes
jules: commit message suggestion: `chore(lint): normalize kale-versions and add test` :thumbsup:
ravi: also filing a tiny RFC: what counts as a legitimate vegetable-themed suffix for versions (cc @jules)
anya: new office policy: any version with more than three dots must be accompanied by an artist statement and at least one emoji
jules: can we get an emoji reaction for "semver survivor"? :bandage:
ops-bot: FYI: previous deploys had similar nonstandard strings, adding a spike ticket to infra backlog (reaction: :memo:)
ravi: side idea: weekly "Compiler Complaints" meetup — bring pastries, gripe about whitespace and semicolons
anya: I'm in. I'll bring stickers that say "I survived YAML"
jules: I'll bring muffins and an eraser for the whiteboard gripes :coffee:
anya: ok closing thread. PR incoming for lint and an absurd commit title.
